source.original_title: 05/27/2026 - Jared Lyons x Andrew Musial KL
source.display_title: 05/27/2026 - Jared Lyons x Andrew Musial KL — Follow Up

setter.name: Kyla
setter.evidence: Rep named her at 00:00:23: 'So I went through everything that you told to my friend, Kaila.' Title suffix KL matches.

prospect.name: Jared Lyons
prospect.occupation: Not stated. Travels constantly for work and describes 'back-to-back meetings all day'; upcoming trips to Mykonos, Ibiza, Saint-Tropez and Marbella.
prospect.training_background: Highly trained. Lifts daily and has done so for years, plus conditioning sessions at The Yard, an F45-founder concept similar to Hyrox. Trains twice a day at times. Completed a Hyrox race in about 1:10 straight off a 15-hour flight to Barcelona, with no specific preparation. Formerly a competitive lacrosse player. Has spent $1,500-$2,000 a month on in-person trainers.
prospect.medical: Two labral tears, one in each shoulder — treated with stem cell injections instead of surgery, which he says helped; still gets shoulder pain under high training volume and high reps. A metal bar and eight screws in his right leg from a lacrosse injury, which rules out long-distance running. Bad flat feet. States 'I don't really let any of these things affect me, at least when I'm working out.'

signals: Opens by ruling out any rescue framing: 'I'm not here to lose 10% of body fat or anything like that. I'm just looking to change it up'
Already fit and plateaued — trains daily, races Hyrox for fun, and wants variety and mobility rather than transformation
Price capacity is explicitly not the barrier: 'it's not even like the $4,000. I spend way more on stupid all the time' and he already spends $1,500-2,000 a month on trainers
Rep classified him the same way on the call: 'Look, man, I'm going to be honest with you. Like, you're not our typical client'
The blocker is product shape rather than price — he wants programming without coaching, which is the opposite of what the offer is built around

goals.text: Change up a gym routine he has been repeating for years and has grown bored with
Break a training plateau — 'I feel like I've like plateaued. I haven't really like grown any'
Be able to get a full equivalent workout anywhere with a single or double kettlebell while travelling
Improve mobility, which he named as the baseline priority
Build a stronger core, the area he admits to neglecting
Keep doing more Hyrox races for enjoyment

pains.text: Two labral tears, one per shoulder, managed with stem cells rather than surgery; pain returns under high volume and reps
Metal bar and eight screws in the right leg, which rules out long-distance running
Bored of the same routine after years and no longer progressing
Constant travel breaks his training and his diet — 'when I'm traveling is kind of like where I really up'
Skips leg day about half the time and neglects core work because he does not enjoy them
Sweet tooth that runs away from him when travelling — 'one bite turns into 20'

objections.raw_quote: What if I don't want to do six months? if I want to just do for, like, two or three months?
objections.rep_response: Immediately named an off-menu tier: 'We don't have two months, to be fair. We have, like, three months... Three months is 4K.'

objections.raw_quote: for me to pay 6K to just get a program seems a little crazy for me. But I get it. I mean, I'm not the average customer, so I get it. It doesn't exactly fit.
objections.rep_response: Challenged it once — 'What's so crazy about it?' — and got a clear answer about product shape rather than money, then did not isolate or take a financial picture.

objections.raw_quote: I spend, you know, 1,500, 2K a month sometimes on trainers when I'm here, not traveling as much. And it's like, I could probably, you know, I don't know, to spend the same amount for virtual seems a little crazy.
objections.rep_response: Not addressed at all. The rep never pointed out that $6,000 over six months is $1,000 a month, less than the prospect's existing in-person trainer spend.

objections.raw_quote: I don't really need or want all this extra stuff. So it's, I guess what I, what I want is not necessarily something that you guys normally sell. Like, I just want to buy a program.
objections.rep_response: Argued that he needs the coaching because he lacks experience in complex kettlebell movements; the prospect conceded month one and refused the rest.

objections.raw_quote: All right, well, I'll think on it. I'll let you guys know. If I was to do it, it definitely would probably be a three-month commitment, not a six or 12. But yeah, let me think on it a bit.
objections.rep_response: Ran one scripted move — 'So what's coming up for you right now that's keeping you from actually moving forward?' — then abandoned the play and proposed a discounted trial instead.

offer.payment_plan_terms: All tiers stated as paid up front: 'That's paid up front.'
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Invented live as a 30-day trial: 'Would you be down for, like, 30 days just checking how it works? And if you're satisfied with that, you would move on? If not?' — which the rep then named: 'We call it love it or leave it.' Clarified as 'you get a full month, you check it out, how it's, if it fits your needs or not, and afterwards, you can leave if you don't like it.' No refund mechanics, terms or conditions were stated.

evidence: Verbal interest in the trial only: 'if there's a 30-day hybrid, I'd be open to that for sure' and 'Yeah, I think that would work'
But no commitment: 'let me just check a few other things and then I will get back to you if I'm going to confirm it'
No payment taken and no payment link sent, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link rule does not apply
Follow-up booked for Friday at 13:00 Pacific after a failed attempt to schedule Thursday

Counter-evidence that this is weaker than it looks: he rejected the actual product twice — 'what I want is not necessarily something that you guys normally sell' — and only warmed once the price fell to a quarter of the original
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call Friday at 13:00 Pacific, invite to be emailed; prospect said he would look at other options first and might answer sooner.

notable.note: The clearest pricing-integrity finding in the batch. Inside roughly four minutes the price moved from $6,000 for six months, to an off-menu $4,000 for three months, to $1,500 for a 30-day 'love it or leave it' trial invented on the call — driven entirely by hesitation, with no financial objection to justify it, since the prospect had stated outright that $4,000 was not the problem. Note the timing: this happened the day after sales operations told this rep on a training call that unapproved payment structures were 'being a little creative' but that 'if we need to get the deal through' he could improvise. Separately, the prospect has two labral tears managed without surgery and was presented overhead ballistic kettlebell training with no clearance question.

quality.notes: Labels invert repeatedly, including the injury disclosures at 00:04:59-00:05:33 where the prospect's account of the metal bar and screws is split across both speakers. At 00:19:57 the price exchange transcribes as '6K. 6K. 5K. 5K.' — most likely a garbled repetition of 6K rather than a separate $5,000 quote, but it cannot be resolved from the text and is recorded here rather than asserted as a price. Prospect's Fathom label is the lowercase handle 'jaredlyons'.
